I study how regulatory DNA controls transcription in plants: where transcription
starts, how much of it happens, and how those decisions change during development
and in response to the environment. My work combines genome-wide assays of
transcription initiation and chromatin, plant genetics, and computational models
of regulatory sequence, and I write and maintain open-source software for the
genomics community.

I am a postdoctoral scientist in [Tatsuya Nobori's group](https://www.tsl.ac.uk/our-work/scientific-groups/tatsuya-nobori-group)
at The Sainsbury Laboratory in Norwich, where I use capped-small RNA sequencing
(csRNA-seq), single-nucleus multiomics and sequence-to-function models to study how
plant cells switch on immune responses. Before that I did my PhD with
[Julia Qüesta](https://www.cragenomica.es/research-groups/epigenetics-and-plant-development)
at CRAG in Barcelona on non-coding transcription during the seed-to-seedling
transition. For my MSc at the University of Waterloo I worked with
[Barbara Moffatt](https://uwaterloo.ca/biology/profiles/barbara-moffatt) on how a
build-up of methylthioadenosine (MTA), a by-product of polyamine and ethylene
synthesis, disrupts sulfur metabolism and reduces fertility in *Arabidopsis*.
